title: Glanceflow: compact card gesture refinement, rollback patterns, and QA acceptance criteria
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Compact glance cards in the Console currently behave inconsistently across input modalities (touch, mouse, keyboard) when interacting with collapse/expand gestures and the new compact density toggle. This causes accidental rollouts and confusion during canary previews. Goal: Deliver a visual and interaction spec that standardizes swipe/drag collapse gestures, provides clear rollback affordances for rollouts, and includes a deterministic QA acceptance checklist. Scope: design microinteractions, motion timing, contrast and focus styles, copy for rollback CTA, and QA test cases. Out of scope: backend rollout API changes and analytics instrumentation (tracked separately).
comments: 2025-02-18 - Aisha: Shared initial Figma flows for compact-card gestures and three collapse patterns (snap-to, progressive friction, and affordance-only). Called out keyboard parity and focus states for screen reader flow.

2025-02-19 - PM (Jonah Lee): Requested explicit rollback callout when a rollout is under 10% to prevent accidental mass rollouts; suggested inline undo with 5s window and a persistent rollback action in the rollout inspector.

2025-02-20 - Eng (Priya Shah): Flagged performance constraints on Android WebView for continuous drag; recommended limiting continuous redraws and using a two-step threshold gesture (drag past 32px then release to commit).

2025-02-21 - Design lead (Marta Kowalski): Redlines attached for contrast (button outline to 3:1 at 12px), motion duration adjusted to 160ms ease-out for collapse and 240ms for expand to feel weighty but snappy. Requested accessibility notes for reduced-motion preference.

2025-02-22 - UX Research (Daniel O.): Ran a five-user probe on commit ambiguity; users favored a tactile snap and microcopy that says "Collapse card" with an undo toast over ambiguous progressive collapse. Adding microcopy to prototype.
2025-02-23 - QA (Ray Chen): Drafted test cases for gesture, keyboard, and aria announcements; noted an edge case where focus is lost after undo toast on Safari—needs dev verification.

2025-02-24 - Marco: Updated prototype to implement two-step threshold, added explicit rollback CTA in rollout inspector, and added reduced-motion variants. Pushed handoff notes to Drive and opened PR reference in links.
2025-02-25 - Aisha: Submitting for formal design review. Requesting sign-off from PM and Eng on threshold values and undo timing. See acceptance criteria below.
acceptance_criteria: Design spec includes explicit interaction model for touch, mouse, and keyboard with annotated thresholds (32px threshold then release), motion timing, and reduced-motion variants.
Microcopy for collapse/expand, undo toast (5s), and rollout inspector rollback CTA is finalized and approved by PM.
Contrast and focus styles meet accessibility minimums (contrast >= 3:1 for compact control outlines, focus ring visible at 2px).
Prototype links and redline PNGs attached for dev implementation; design tokens for spacing, durations, and easing provided.
QA checklist created and executed by QA on Chrome, Safari, iOS Safari, Android WebView; known issue tracked if focus loss persists on Safari with a linked ticket.
Engineering confirms no regression on continuous redraw budgets and agrees to two-step threshold implementation or an agreed alternative.
PM approves rollout messaging and rollback CTA placement for canary workflows.
next_steps: Design: Resolve two outstanding redline contrast comments and publish final spec (by 2025-02-27).
Engineering: Review and comment on prototype performance trade-offs; confirm implementation plan for two-step threshold and undo toast hooks (by 2025-02-28).
QA: Run acceptance criteria checklist across supported browsers and upload results to Drive; file follow-up ticket if Safari focus loss reproduces (by 2025-03-03).
PM: Approve rollout messaging and schedule canary (by 2025-02-28).
